name: PALS's Notes component kit
summary: Python generators for PALS's Notes scenes (scene-render 1.1/1.2): helpers and components that write inline XML, vendored into each project with a lock file.

requires.brand_kit: palsnotes-brand.xml (passed in by the project; the source of truth for tokens and styles)

extracted_from: v013-jev-decisions (film/lib.py, brand.py, captions.py, shorts.py, emblems.py), byte-identical golden: tests/golden/. mesh and figure generalized from v014-bayonet-charge-2011 (film/trees.py's tube-mesh engine, film/figures.py's articulated rig) — not byte-identical, no golden: v014's own figures.py keeps its rifle-soldier look and is unchanged by this.. audio generalized from v015-short-pack (film/core.py's cue guard, tools/foley.py, qa/tail.py): its twenty scene documents' audio assets and tracks are reproduced byte for byte, and its foley files and ending figures identically

components.name: Doc
components.summary: The document under construction: frame size, text-role styles, id set and the registries that become sections (assets, paints, materials, fields, bodies).
rules: one id set per document: every helper's ids are unique

components.name: bind
components.summary: The helpers with a Doc filled in (uid, text_asset, label, draw, rect, disc, group, pill, Cam, Brand) plus the pure ones.

components.name: f / esc / keys / opacity / path_d / hash01 / fmt / Ids
components.summary: Number formatting (3 decimals, no trailing zeros), attribute escaping, unique ids, opacity windows with fades, keyframe <animate>s, polyline path data, a stable hash shared with expressions (HASH_EXPR).
params: opacity(a, b, fin=0.5, fout=0.5, peak=1.0, ease_in=cubic-out, ease_out=cubic-in)

components.name: palette
components.summary: The kit's colour tokens as hex (INK, RAISED, CREAM, MUTED, ORANGE, RULE, COOL); tokens(kit) reads a kit, check(kit) compares.
rules: palsnotes-brand.xml is the source of truth for tokens (guide §14, Brand)

components.name: text_asset
components.summary: A <text> asset registered once per distinct text and look; returns (id, width, height) with an estimated box.
rules: every text sets its colour explicitly (guide §14: a textStyle colour renders white)

components.name: label
components.summary: A text layer anchored center|left|right, fading in and out over [a, b], optional textAnimator preset.
rules: labels >= 36 px at 1080p (guide §5, Typography): smaller sizes are raised to 36

components.name: draw
components.summary: A frame-sized path that draws itself (trimEnd) from a over dur, then stays until b.

components.name: rect / disc / group
components.summary: A centred (or top-left anchored) rect, a circle, a group of items with an optional fade.
params: rect(x, y, w, h, fill, a, b, radius, stroke, sw, anchor)
disc(x, y, r, fill, a, b, stroke)

components.name: pill
components.summary: A fully rounded rect with a centred caps label, one group anchored at its centre (ids pid, pid-b, pid-t).
rules: orange is a fill here, never type on a raised panel (kit contrast note)

components.name: arrow_d / round_rect_d
components.summary: Path data: an arrow with an open head; a rounded rectangle (the emblems' rr).

components.name: Cam
components.summary: A 2D camera group for one act: framing cues keyed to times or beats (through an injected resolver), clamped to safe rectangles, sine-in-out moves that lead their cue, a drift after each cue; verify() samples every 0.25 s.
rules: safe-rect clamp: what must stay in frame is kept 150 x 84 px inside the frame (guide §14, Camera)
widening moves lead, narrowing moves wait for the old content to fade (guide §14)
verify every 0.25 s against the safe rect in force and that of the last 1.2 s; builds report breaches (guide §14)
no shot holds still: drift after each cue unless hold (guide §5, Cinematography)

components.name: prologue
components.summary: The kit's prologue (parameters, styles, layouts, safe areas, font asset, text assets, symbols, accessibility) verbatim, with the episode's parameter defaults.
rules: every episode carries the kit's prologue verbatim, defaults set per episode (guide §14, Brand)

components.name: Brand.title_card
components.summary: Opening title over ink: kicker (pn-label) at 192,300, title (pn-display, balanced, <= 3 lines) rising into 192,360, optional line-drawn emblem, notch.
rules: inline copy, not a symbol instance: <override> is dropped by encode (guide §6, Avoid 1)
composited above the finish (guide §14, Brand)
title card before 20 s (guide §14): timing is the caller's

components.name: Brand.chapter_card
components.summary: Chapter divider over ink: orange number (pn-number) at 192,340, rule at y 520, title (pn-heading, <= 2 lines) at 192,540, optional emblem.
rules: inline copy above the finish (guide §6, §14)

components.name: Brand.lower_third
components.summary: Raised panel with an orange bar at 192,680, 900 x 152: name (pn-heading) and role (pn-label), sliding in from x 160.
rules: clear of the caption band; orange is never type on the raised panel (kit)

components.name: Brand.source_line
components.summary: Citation line (pn-cite, <= 2 lines) at 192,108, top-left inside title safe.
rules: kit sizes: pn-cite 24 px labels a source, it does not inform (guide §5)

components.name: Brand.end_card
components.summary: End card over ink: next-video label at 192,480 and credit lines, drifting up; right two thirds left free for end-screen elements; notch.
rules: inline copy above the finish (guide §14)

components.name: Brand.notch / Brand.ink / Brand.emblem
components.summary: The brand mark (orange right triangle, 64 px, bottom-left), a full-frame ink field, a line-drawn subject that draws on stroke by stroke and drifts.

components.name: split_cues / sidecar
components.summary: Caption cues from [(word, start, end)]: units at sentence ends and pauses > 0.45 s, split into the fewest two-line cues by reading rate; no break (between cues or lines) after a weak word, inside a number (one in ten, twenty thousand, 75 per cent) or inside a name (Apollo 12) while another break fits (no_break, line_break); no stubs; a cue the pauses cannot hold for 1 s joins a neighbour; the <captions> sidecar track with word timings.
rules: captions <= 2 x 42 characters, <= 17 characters/s (guide §4, §13, §14 QA gates)
split at clause ends (guide §14)

components.name: timed / stats
components.summary: Display windows: each cue shown for at least len/16.5 s and never under 1 s (MIN_SHOW), held after its last word first (up to HOLD, 1 s), then started early by at most LEAD (0.30 s; FIRST_LEAD 0.35 s for the first cue), never overlapping the next cue; stats() reports cues over 17 cps and the longest line.
rules: readable at 17 characters/s (guide §5, Duration)

components.name: short_cues
components.summary: A Short's burned active-word cues in output time from film words and segment maps; no cue before the cover lifts.
rules: Shorts burn karaoke/active-word captions (guide §9)
captions <= 2 lines

components.name: shorts.overlay
components.summary: A Short's overlay symbol in output time: cover card for 0.8 s (ink, subject, notch), headline rising into the top band, ink bands and feathers around the fitted picture, hook to the long video for the last 2.6 s. The subject drawing is injected.
rules: the first frame is the cover (thumbnail.md)
nothing essential above y 220 on a cover (thumbnail.md, Shorts grid)

components.name: shorts.span_times / segments / output_xml / build
components.summary: Film spans that start and end in narration pauses, output segments with 0.3 s crossfades, the Short <output> with its burned caption track, and the whole set with the feather paints and the 9:16 fit layout.
rules: Shorts are output segments of the film's document (SREP 13)

components.name: physics.signature / physics.block
components.summary: The <physics> block, pointing at a simulation cache only when the cache was made for this document's rigid bodies and fields.

components.name: mesh.tapered_tube / mesh.bake_bone / mesh.Mesh / mesh.rot_towards
components.summary: A tapered tube along a 3D polyline, baked once to assets/*.obj and referenced by <object3D primitive="mesh">, for geometry no native primitive covers (a native capsule is one uniform radius). Pure standard library, no numpy: baking is offline, not per-frame.
params: tapered_tube(length, r0, r1, sides=10, segs=6, bulge=0.0, seed=None, up=False)
bake_bone(out_dir, name, length, r0, r1, ..., up=False) -> mesh id, cached per (out_dir, name)
rules: OBJ is Y-up metres; the scene imports a mesh as (100x, -100y, -100z) (guide, confirmed against v014's world.py/trees.py)

up=False (the default) grows the tube away from the root (a limb bone); up=True grows it toward the root (a torso rising from a spine joint at pelvis height) — get this backward and the bone points away from its joint, not into it; caught on a render, not a reading of the code

components.name: figure.figure / figure.bone_meshes / figure.default_materials / figure.POSES / figure.DIMS
components.summary: An articulated 3D figure (stand, walk, run, crouch, kneel-fire, prone) following a ground path at a cadence set by the pose, built from pnkit.mesh's tapered bones so it holds up closer to camera than a uniform-capsule rig. Generalized from v014-bayonet-charge-2011's film/figures.py (a rifle soldier) — this module's own POSES are sized for empty hands, not copied from that rifle-carrying figure's.
params: figure(fid, segments [(t0, t1, mode, path)], x0, z0, mesh_ids, materials, heading0=0, dims=DIMS, poses=POSES, head_accessory=None, chest_accessory=None, extra_y=None)
bone_meshes(assets_dir, dims=DIMS) -> (mesh_ids, asset_xml), bake once per document
default_materials() -> (ids, xml) — a plain unarmed look; pass your own for a specific one
rules: every pose table's joint-angle signs are copied from v014's, not re-derived (guide: the engine's positive rotationX swings a hanging limb's end forward; the sign per joint is empirically tuned, not a clean rule)
a carried object (a rifle, a tool) needs its own `poses` with bent elbows, as v014's did — this module's defaults hang the arms

components.name: vo.speak / vo.hazards / vo.rules / vo.entries / vo.asr_aliases / vo.asr_normalise / vo.asr_currency / vo.lexicon
components.summary: The narration dictionary by language (pnkit/data/vo_lexicon.json: respellings, rules, Whisper aliases, each with its source). speak() applies the respellings; hazards() lists what a TTS engine is likely to misread before synthesis (a period that splits a word, digits, symbols, untested acronyms, over-long sentences); asr_normalise() makes known mis-hearings compare equal in the word-error check.
params: asr_currency(text): '$450 billion' -> '450 billion dollars', for both sides of the word-error check, before the number speller
lang: BCP 47 as the projects use it (en, pt-br); a base language falls back (en-us -> en)
rules: abbreviations without periods in the spoken text: AI, not A.I. (guide §12 step 3, observed in v013)
numbers written as words in the spoken text; the screen and captions keep digits (guide §5)
a bad Kokoro reading is fixed by changing the text, never by re-rolling (guide §14)
test a new term with tools/vo_probe.py before adding it

components.name: audio.Cues / audio.AudioDesignError / audio.library / audio.cue / audio.retired / audio.tail_ok / audio.resolve_digest / audio.scene_cues / audio.scene_tail_violations
components.summary: A film's sound cues, held to the audio-design rule (user, 2026-10-01: each film its own sound design; nothing laser-like). Cues collects effects and beds from the channel's palette (pnkit/data/sfx_library.json: AudioForge cues and tools/foley.py's files), refuses retired pitch sweeps and synthetic stings by name, refuses anything but soft struck foley in the ending, and writes the <audio>/<generated> assets and <audioTrack>s. scene_cues and scene_tail_violations read the cues back from a scene document.
params: Cues(extra=None, tail_lead=0.5, end_guard=1.0): extra = {name: {kind: audioforge|file, model/prompt or path, gain, tail_ok}} for a project's own cues
sfx(t, name, gain=None); ambience(name, gain=None, fade_in=1.2)
assets(duration, tag='film', digest=None, cache_dir='sfx'); tracks(duration, bus='fx-bus', duck='vo-bus')
rules: no laser-like sound: no pitch sweep, no synthetic sting, no sustained pure high tone; down, riser, pop, success and tone are retired and a film that names one fails at build time
after the last word minus 0.5 s only soft struck foley may start (tick, click, stamp, paper, pin, shutter, tap, tok, thud, step, clunk, slide, scratch); then the music resolves
each film gets its own sound design from its own world: a bed where the place has one, and a cue for what is seen to happen; do not reuse one ending gesture across a set
a bed is cut to the film with its fades baked in: a track's fadeOut acts at the end of its asset, not of the document
a cue that would start in the film's last second is dropped
verify the encoded file with tools/tail_check.py: held pure partial at most 0.4 s, mean share at most 30 %, no glide, the last 0.1 s at least 15 dB under the level 2 s earlier

components.name: vo.speak_map / vo.pt_number / vo.pt_cardinal
components.summary: Numbers and the token-level written -> spoken map. speak(..., numbers=True) writes digits as pt-BR words (12,4% -> doze vírgula quatro por cento; 2003 -> dois mil e três) and speak_map() returns SpeakMap(written, spoken, tokens): for each written token the spoken words it became (lexicon respellings and numbers), which written_words() uses to time captions. speak() without numbers is unchanged.
params: speak_map(text, lang, engine='kokoro', numbers=False) -> SpeakMap(written, spoken, tokens[MapToken(written, spoken, start, end)])
engine: any | kokoro | chatterbox | piper | elevenlabs (the lexicon's engine field); numbers=True is pt-br only
rules: captions show the written text and are timed by the spoken words; never rebuild captions from the spoken text (Lula 3.0.0: 'DOZE VÍRGULA QUATRO ...')
ElevenLabs letter-name respellings (ABC -> á bê cê) are approved by ear: Whisper cannot verify letter names
OAS and TSE are read correctly as written by ElevenLabs; leave them

components.name: captions.written_words / captions.CaptionAlignError
components.summary: Caption words in the written form from the timed spoken words of a TTS alignment: '12,4%' carries the start of 'doze' and the end of 'cento'. Uses vo.speak_map, so the alignment follows a map, not a guess, and raises CaptionAlignError naming the written token when the spoken words do not match (a stale or edited text).
params: written_words(spoken_words [(word, start, end)], written_text, lang, engine='kokoro', numbers=None) -> [(word, start, end)]
pass the engine the audio was made with; numbers=None is on for pt, off otherwise
rules: compare by letters and digits only: case, accents kept, punctuation ignored
a punctuation-only token is joined to the previous word
no silent repair: a mismatch raises

components.name: captions.check_text / captions.Finding
components.summary: The caption text gate: the cues' joined text must equal the approved written text (only whitespace and line breaks normalised), and for pt-br no cue may spell out 'vírgula', 'por cento' or a number the approved text writes in digits.
params: cues: strings, {'text': ...}, word lists, (word, start, end) lists or timed cues (words, start, end)
rules: run it on the finished cues before delivery, against the approved text, never against a text derived from the cues or from the spoken text

components.name: pixel.view_outside / pixel.ViewOutside / pixel.figure_cut / pixel.plate_line_breaks / pixel.scale_off_grid
components.summary: Build-time checks for integer-grid pixel-art films: the region a zoom/pan view shows and how much lies outside the set; a sprite crop through the torso with nothing over the cut; a plate line that ends in a colon or arrow or leaves a value alone; a scale that breaks the pixel grid.
params: view_outside(set_w, set_h, grid_w, grid_h, zoom, cx, cy, anchor=None, tol=0.5) -> ViewOutside(x0, y0, x1, y1, cols, rows, fraction; .outside, .describe())
figure_cut(sprite_h, crop_row, occluded=False) -> finding string or None
rules: a zoom/pan view must stay inside the set: the rest renders as flat background (Lula 3.0.0 scene 11a)
a sprite is not cropped between 35 % and 85 % of its height unless something covers the cut
a plate line does not end in ':' or an arrow and a label is not parted from its value
scales keep the integer grid

components.name: files.write_once / files.next_free / files.write_next / files.WriteOnceError
components.summary: Approved files are write-once: write_once creates a path atomically and raises WriteOnceError (a FileExistsError) if anything is there, even a dangling symlink; next_free returns the path itself when free, else the first of stem-v2.ext, stem-v3.ext, ...; write_next writes to the first free path and returns it.
rules: a file the owner approved is never overwritten by a re-run: write the new version beside it with a suffix

components.name: ctx.Ctx / ctx.set_timings / ctx.timings / ctx.slot / ctx.PlanError / ctx.Geometry / ctx.P / ctx.lettering / ctx.text_width
components.summary: The build context of an integer-grid pixel-art film (320 x 180 cells, 6 px each): scenes, shots, zoom (integer scale), plates and boxes, signs, actors and crowds, steam, dust, tint; finish() checks plates against signs and figures. Extracted from Lula 3.0.0 (work/art3/v3/common.py); the 32 Lula scenes build byte-identical against it.
rules: picture above row 146, soles at or above 145
integer-pixel motion only
ids carry the scene prefix
same input, same bytes

components.name: sets.school_street / sets.table_room / sets.table_pieces / sets.house_exterior / sets.house_interior / sets.bairro
components.summary: Shared pixel-art sets of the Lula film (the full list is in the module), each 320 x 180 or wider for a pan, deterministic (palette snapping sorts its candidates).

components.name: checks.CheckedCtx / checks.apply_waivers
components.summary: Build-time picture checks run on unchanged scene modules: zoom-window-outside-set, figure-cut-mid-body, plate-line-break (judged by pnkit.pixel); waivers need a reason.
rules: PALS-Notes/docs/reviews/2026-10-07/PICTURE-REVIEW.md section 2

components.name: plan.parse_plan / plan.check_plan_only / plan.check_plan_slots / plan.check_built
components.summary: The picture plan check (Lula check_plan.py) as functions: the plan's own stacking, its slots against the timings, built shots against plan and timings.

components.name: frames.flat_field / frames.plate_visible / frames.to_grid / frames.parse_rgb
components.summary: Checks on rendered frames: flat or empty field (thresholds judged by eye on about 12 frames, not a precision study) and a plate card visible in the frame.

components.name: segment.check / segment.near_static_spans / segment.first_frame_defects / segment.black_or_flat / segment.geometry_problems
components.summary: The per-segment render check run on the render host after each encode (Lula check_scene_v3.py), plus flat field on each shot's first frame and plate visibility.

components.name: timings.load_sentences / timings.diff
components.summary: The word-timings file in either shape, and the diff of two versions (moved sentences and words); the core of tools/timings_diff.py.

components.name: config.Film / config.FilmError / config.check_timings
components.summary: film.json: the one file that drives a film's build; remote paths relative to the host's $HOME (no '~').
rules: PALS-Notes/docs/reviews/2026-10-07/PIPELINE-REVIEW.md section 4

components.name: stages.Build / stages.run / stages.table / stages.ORDER
components.summary: film_build's restartable, hash-recorded stages: snapshot, voice, plan, generate, assemble, render, audio, join, gates, sheets, pack.
rules: heavy work only on the render hosts, under the lock
a full render is write-once (name-vN.mp4)
one timings file
GATES.md is generated from the gate JSON

components.name: gates.judge / gates.gates_md / gates.parse_ebur128 / gates.parse_blackdetect / gates.psnr / gates.voice_margins
components.summary: The film gates as data: parse the measures, judge them against film.json, write GATES.md.

components.name: voice.pronounce_terms / voice.build_timings
components.summary: The pronunciation list (acronyms, numerals, names, listed terms) before any synthesis, and the film's timings from the takes (written words, spoken times).

tools.tools/sync.py PROJECT_DIR: vendor pnkit into PROJECT_DIR/film/vendor/pnkit and write film/vendor/pnkit.lock
tools.tools/check_lock.py PROJECT_DIR: verify the vendored copy against its lock
tools.tools/gate.py SCENE [--probe T ...] [--m: validate --deny-warnings, eval at probe times (default 0 s) and once per layout and variant (E05/E06 override/target errors), flash-check state
tools.tools/vo_probe.py LINE|FILE ... [--lang: Kokoro reads each line, Whisper large-v3 hears it back, internal pauses over 0.25 s are listed (run in the voice venv); test a term before adding it to the VO dictionary
tools.tools/foley.py [OUT_DIR]: synthesise the palette's own sounds (tap, tok, thud, tink, clunk, chime, step, swish, settle, rumble, cascade; beds under, hum, roomlarge) into OUT_DIR (default sfx/custom): deterministic, with a self-check for gliding tones (run in the voice venv)
tools.tools/tail_check.py MEDIA --voice-end T|: measure an encoded film's ending against the audio-design rule: the cues that start in it, the longest held pure partial, glides, the decay (run in the voice venv); exits 1 on CHECK
tools.tools/caption_gate.py CUES --approved TE: the caption text gate as a CLI: CUES is .vtt, a scene .xml (every <cue text>) or .json; exit 1 on findings, 2 on unreadable input
tools.tools/timings_diff.py A.json B.json [--t: sentences and words whose start or end moved by more than the threshold; simple format [{sentence, text, words [[word, start, end]]}] or the Lula timings-v2.json shape; exit 1 when anything moved
tools.tools/flat_field.py --bg COLOUR FRAME.pn: report frames whose picture is mostly the background colour (empty-background) or one flat colour (flat-field) on the film's logical grid; thresholds judged by eye on about 12 frames, not a precision study; needs Pillow; run on the first rendered frame of each shot
flag an <instance> with no start whose symbol reads time in a condition (arbitrary first frame); gate.py runs it and prints a line only on a finding
tools.tools/cue_drift.py --markers M.json --ti: compare a score's word-tied cue markers with the film's current word timings (generic JSON format in the docstring); exit 1 when a marker is over --tol seconds off or lost; --format lula --score-timings OLD --film-timings NEW --make-score make_score.py reads the Lula score's c.at() markers
tools.tools/vm_preflight.py [HOST ...] [--min-: before a render batch: reachability, free disk, who holds or waits on ~/heavy.lock, CPU model per host (warns when they differ) and a cross-VM frame sha256 probe; one table plus a JSON report; exit 1 on an unreachable host, low disk, a failed render or disagreeing hosts
build a film from film.json in restartable, hash-recorded stages; prints one summary table
tools.tools/pixelart/lula_alias.py V3_DIR TIMI: build Lula 3.0.0 scene modules against pnkit.pixelart (or the film's own framework) and print each scene's sha256
